t: The project for flood protection on Fourmile Run, city of Alexandria and Arlington County, Virginia, approved by resolutions of the Committees on Public Works of the United States Senate and House of Representatives, dated June 25, 1970, and July 14, 1970, respectively, in accordance with the provisions of section 201 of the Flood Control Act of 1965 (Public Law 89–298), is hereby modified to provide that the Secretary of the Army, acting through the Chief of Engineers, shall replace the George Washington Memorial Park-way bridge over Fourmile Run, at Federal expense, substantially as recommended by the Chief of Engineers in his report dated March 2, 1970, published as House Document Numbered 91–358.

fable.w: The section modifies a flood protection project to direct the Secretary of the Army to replace a bridge at federal expense. The tempting reading is that the committee resolutions and the Chief of Engineers' recommendation amount to consultation, but Congress's committees and the Chief of Engineers are all inside the federal government. The city of Alexandria and Arlington County are named only as the project's location, and no outside party is given a role, hearing, comment opportunity, or right to sue.
fable.s: substantially as recommended by the Chief of Engineers in his report dated March 2, 1970

qwen_block.w: The section describes a project modification based on resolutions from congressional committees and a report from the Chief of Engineers. Congress and federal agencies are inside the federal government. There is no requirement for consultation with or participation by outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities in the decision-making process described.
qwen_block.s: approved by resolutions of the Committees on Public Works of the United States Senate and House of Representatives

opus.w: Every actor in this section is inside the federal government: congressional committees approved the project, and the Secretary of the Army and the Chief of Engineers carry it out. Alexandria and Arlington County are named only as places, not as parties to be consulted, so no outside party takes part in the decision to replace the bridge. There is also no comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.
opus.s: approved by resolutions of the Committees on Public Works of the United States Senate and House of Representatives
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this is participation because the project was "approved by resolutions of the Committees on Public Works" of Congress, and because it names the city of Alexandria and Arlington County. That reading fails. Congressional committees are inside the federal government. The local governments appear only as the project's location; they are not consulted about any decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes a project modification based on resolutions from Congressional committees and recommendations from the Chief of Engineers. Both Congress and federal agency officials are inside the federal government. There is no requirement for consultation with or participation by state, local, tribal, or private entities in the decision-making process described here.
qwen_chat.s: approved by resolutions of the Committees on Public Works of the United States Senate and House of Representatives... substantially as recommended by the Chief of Engineers in his report
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the project was "approved by resolutions of the Committees on Public Works," this involves participation. However, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so their approval is an internal legislative act, not participation by an outside party. Furthermore, the modification relies on a report by the Chief of Engineers (a federal official), which is intra-governmental coordination.
